card: This PR updates SignPSBTInput to accept valid 65-byte Taproot signatures when PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE is not explicitly specified. Currently, an omitted sighash field defaults to SIGHASH_DEFAULT (64 bytes), rejecting valid self-describing 65-byte signatures and causing finalization failures on valid transactions. This fixes issue #36507, allowing workflows with external signers or mixed sighash types across script paths to process cleanly while maintaining strict validation when explicit sighash constraints are set.
changed_since_previous: Now includes the complete implementation in `src/psbt.cpp` and comprehensive unit and functional regression tests covering key-path, script-path, and mixed sighash spends.
evidence: Issue #36507 reported that `SignPSBTInput` rejects valid 65-byte Taproot script signatures when `PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE` is absent.
BIP 341 defines Taproot signatures as either 64 bytes (implying `SIGHASH_DEFAULT`) or 65 bytes (specifying explicit sighashes), while BIP 371 makes `PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE` optional.
problem: When a Taproot PSBT input lacks the optional `PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE` field, `SignPSBTInput` defaults to expecting `SIGHASH_DEFAULT` (64 bytes). Valid 65-byte signatures produced with explicit sighashes (such as `SIGHASH_ALL`) are rejected with `SIGHASH_MISMATCH`, preventing valid PSBTs—including multisig inputs with mixed sighashes—from being signed or finalized.

risk.why: A logic error in PSBT sighash validation could permit malformed signatures or prevent legitimate Taproot transactions from being signed or finalized.

summary: Updates `SignPSBTInput` to allow valid 65-byte Taproot signatures (which self-encode an explicit sighash type) when no `PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE` or caller option is specified. Previously, absent sighash fields caused Taproot inputs to assume `SIGHASH_DEFAULT` and reject any signature other than 64 bytes. Strict sighash checking remains enforced whenever an explicit sighash type is specified.
